title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is a voice and video impersonation carried out over a consumer messaging app. The synthetic likeness of a public figure was used to open a conversation, and the fraud then ran through a chain of supposed officials, a manager, then a CBI officer, each demanding a payment. The deepfake was the entry point rather than the whole scheme. The money moved because the victim believed he was speaking to a chief minister and then to investigators.

The failure sits at the point of contact, not inside any system the victim could inspect. A WhatsApp video call offers no provenance signal to the person receiving it, and the reporting describes no verification step on the platform side that would have flagged a synthetic public figure. Catching this would have required either a caller-identity check the recipient could see, or the victim independently confirming the offer through an official channel before paying. The reporting does not say whether either was available to him.

What is not established is who produced the deepfake, how it was made, or whether anyone has been identified or charged. A police case has been registered under the Information Technology Act, and a registered case is not a finding of guilt. The reporting gives one outlet's account of a complaint, and the identity of the caller remains unverified.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old security guard in Bengaluru named Ratikanta Giri received a WhatsApp video call on September 9 from someone using an AI-generated deepfake to pose as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The caller offered him Rs 11 lakh in financial aid, then had a supposed manager tell him Rs 5 lakh was allotted and ask for fees. Giri paid Rs 5,000, then Rs 18,000 when told his PIN was locked, and later over Rs 50,000 to a person claiming to be a CBI officer demanding a fine. He transferred more than Rs 1.04 lakh in total before refusing a further Rs 50,000 demand and realizing he was duped.

Giri contacted the cybercrime helpline 1930 and then approached Byappanahalli police, who registered a case under the Information Technology Act. This is the first such deepfake case reported in the city. Fraudsters sent him a letter claiming Rs 5 lakh was allotted and identity proof of a purported CBI officer. A senior officer urged people not to believe such calls or make payments based on such claims.
